**Vision:** Rewrite the AutoIt character-by-character paste tool as a modern Tauri desktop app with an animated Yeti SVG character that watches text input and covers its eyes when masking is enabled. Compact UI with multi-slot clipboard and global hotkeys.

## Success Criteria

- App launches as a compact Tauri window with Yeti SVG animation
- Yeti eyes follow text input cursor position
- Yeti covers eyes when mask toggle is activated
- Text is typed character-by-character into the active window after a delay
- Multi-slot clipboard allows storing and recalling multiple text snippets
- Global hotkeys trigger paste without switching windows
- Window stays small and unobtrusive

- [x] **S01: Tauri Scaffold + Yeti SVG Animation** `risk:medium` `depends:[]`
  > After this: App launches showing animated Yeti with text input. Eyes follow cursor as you type.

- [x] **S02: Core Paste Functionality (Character-by-Character)** `risk:high` `depends:[S01]`
  > After this: Enter text, click paste, text appears character-by-character in another window after 1.5s delay.

- [x] **S03: Mask Toggle + Yeti Eye Covering** `risk:low` `depends:[S01]`
  > After this: Click mask button → input becomes password field, Yeti covers eyes with arms. Click again → unmask, arms drop.

- [x] **S04: Multi-Slot Clipboard + Global Hotkeys** `risk:medium` `depends:[S02]`
  > After this: Store text in 3 slots, switch between them. Use global hotkey to trigger paste from any app.

## Boundary Map

```\nTauri App\n├── Frontend (HTML/CSS/JS)\n│   ├── Yeti SVG Animation (GSAP)\n│   ├── Text Input Field\n│   ├── Mask Toggle Button\n│   └── Clipboard Slot Selector\n└── Backend (Rust)\n    ├── Keyboard Simulation (SendInput)\n    ├── Global Hotkey Registration\n    └── Clipboard Slot Storage\n```

# S02: Core Paste Functionality (Character-by-Character)

**Goal:** Implement character-by-character paste into target windows via Rust backend keyboard simulation.
**Demo:** Enter text, click paste, text appears character-by-character in another window after 1.5s delay.

## Must-Haves

- Text entered in input is typed char-by-char into the target window after a configurable delay. Paste button triggers the operation. Status feedback shown in UI.

## Proof Level

- This slice proves: functional — text typed into target window character by character

## Integration Closure

Core paste feature end-to-end. Frontend button triggers Rust command that sends keystrokes.

## Verification

- Console logging of each keystroke sent. Status feedback in UI.

## Tasks

- [x] **T01: Implement Rust type_text command with Windows SendInput** `est:30m`
  Add a Tauri command `type_text` in main.rs that takes a string and a delay_ms parameter. Use the Windows SendInput API (via winapi crate or raw FFI) to simulate keyboard input character by character. Each character is sent as a Unicode keypress event (KEYBDINPUT with KEYEVENTF_UNICODE). Sleep for delay_ms between each character. Add a 1.5s initial delay before typing starts (so user can switch to target window).
  - Files: `src-tauri/src/main.rs`, `src-tauri/Cargo.toml`
  - Verify: cargo build succeeds. Invoke type_text from frontend, text appears in Notepad.

- [x] **T02: Wire frontend paste button to Tauri command with status feedback** `est:20m`
  Wire the Paste button in index.html to call the Tauri type_text command. Use the Tauri JS API (window.__TAURI__.core.invoke) to call the Rust backend. Show a countdown or status indicator while the initial delay runs. Disable the button during typing. Re-enable when done.
  - Files: `src/index.html`, `src/app.js`
  - Verify: Click paste button, switch to Notepad within 1.5s, text appears character-by-character.

# S01: Hotkey persistence fix

**Load the settings store from disk at startup so the persisted hotkey wins over the default.**

## What Happened

Root cause: main.rs called app.get_store at setup time. In tauri-plugin-store 2.x, get_store is a cache-only lookup that returns None when no webview has yet called store.load. decisions.choice: Adapt the vYetti SVG animation (GSAP/TweenMax) from William Lam's vyetti-vsphere-client-customization project
decisions.rationale: The original Yeti animation by Darin S uses SVG + GSAP for eye-tracking on text input and arm-covering on password focus. This maps perfectly to our use case: eyes follow text input, arms cover eyes when masking is toggled.

decisions.decision: How to ensure focus in target application after Alt+Tab window switch
decisions.choice: Save cursor position before Alt+Tab, click at that position after window switch to ensure input focus in target app
decisions.rationale: Alt+Tab alone activates the window but doesn't guarantee cursor focus in the input area (e.g. console windows require a click). User positions cursor in target first, then switches to VCP — clicking back at the saved position restores focus exactly where intended.
